bugs.title: find_duplicates destroys stored records (replaces the store with the de-duplicated valid records)
bugs.expected: find_duplicates leaves the store untouched: count() and all_transactions() return the same results before and after the call.
bugs.actual: After find_duplicates() a store of 4 records (ids A, '', A, B-with-zero-amount) reports count() == 1.
bugs.evidence: Line 54 `self._transactions = unique` assigns the locally built list back to the store. For ids A, B, A, C the store shrinks from 4 records to 3.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_app.py::test_find_duplicates_leaves_the_store_unchanged tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k 'leaves_the_store_unchanged or bh001'
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED. Existing test: all_transactions() after the call has 3 records instead of 4. New test: `assert 1 == 4` for count() after the call on a 4-record store (2 invalid records and 1 duplicate were deleted).

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 54 `self._transactions = unique` writes the method's working list back over the store, so a query method replaces every stored record with the first valid record per id. Symptoms: count(), all_transactions() and every later calculation change after any call (including the CLI summary, which calls find_duplicates last).

fix.summary: Removed the line `self._transactions = unique` from find_duplicates so the method no longer writes to the store.

verification.targeted: PASSED (2 passed): tests/test_app.py::test_find_duplicates_leaves_the_store_unchanged and tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py::test_bh001_find_duplicates_keeps_duplicate_and_invalid_records_in_the_store. Related run `-k duplicates`: 3 passed, 6 failed; the 6 failures are BH-002 reproductions (including test_bh001_bh002_find_duplicates_can_be_called_twice_with_the_same_result, which needs BH-002).
verification.full_suite: 35 passed, 39 failed of 74 after this fix. In tests/test_app.py 7 tests fail, all of which failed at baseline; no baseline-passing test regressed.

bugs.title: find_duplicates returns the first occurrence of each id instead of the repeated records
bugs.expected: Returns every valid record whose id already appeared in an earlier valid record, in insertion order; the first record with an id is not returned; no duplicates gives []. Example: ids A, B, A, C, A return the third and fifth records.
bugs.actual: Returns the first valid record of each id (the originals), never the repeats.
bugs.evidence: Lines 51-53 append a record to `unique` when its id has NOT been seen, and line 55 returns `unique`.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_app.py::test_find_duplicates_returns_the_repeated_record tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k 'returns_the_repeated_record or bh002 or cli_duplicates'
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED. Existing test: 3 records returned (A, B, C originals) instead of [second A]. Spec example A, B, A, C, A returned the first A, B, C instead of the third and fifth records. No-duplicate store returned 3 records instead of []. CLI `duplicates` printed 4 lines instead of 1.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: the loop (lines 51-53) collects a record when its id has not been seen, which builds the list of originals, and line 55 returns that list; the records whose id was already seen are never collected. Symptoms: wrong result from find_duplicates, 'Duplicate records: 4' in the CLI summary and 4 lines from the CLI `duplicates` command.

fix.summary: find_duplicates now collects a valid record when its id was already seen in an earlier valid record (otherwise it remembers the id) and returns that list; the local list was renamed from `unique` to `duplicates` because it no longer holds unique records.

verification.targeted: PASSED (5 passed): tests/test_app.py::test_find_duplicates_returns_the_repeated_record, the three test_bh002_* tests and test_bh001_bh002_find_duplicates_can_be_called_twice_with_the_same_result. Related run `-k duplicates`: 9 passed, 0 failed (includes test_cli_duplicates_prints_the_second_txn_1002_record_only).
verification.full_suite: 41 passed, 33 failed of 74 after this fix. In tests/test_app.py 6 tests fail, all of which failed at baseline; no baseline-passing test regressed.

bugs.title: average_transaction_value raises ZeroDivisionError when there are no valid transactions
bugs.expected: With no valid transactions (including an empty store) it returns 0.0, and it never raises for a store that holds only dictionaries.
bugs.expected_behaviour_source: demo-app/EXPECTED_BEHAVIOUR.md section `average_transaction_value()` (lines 87-88); app.py table row `--empty summary` (line 132)
bugs.actual: Raises ZeroDivisionError whenever there is no valid transaction.
bugs.evidence: Line 44 `return round_money(total / len(valid))` has no guard for len(valid) == 0.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_app.py::test_average_of_empty_store_is_zero tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k 'average_of_empty_store or bh003 or cli_empty_summary'
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at transaction_service.py:44, for an empty store, for a store holding only invalid records, and through `app.py --empty summary`.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 44 divides by len(valid) with no guard for an empty list of valid transactions. Symptom: ZeroDivisionError from average_transaction_value and from `app.py --empty summary`.

fix.summary: average_transaction_value returns 0.0 before the division when the list of valid transactions is empty.

verification.targeted: PASSED (3 passed): tests/test_app.py::test_average_of_empty_store_is_zero, test_bh003_average_with_only_invalid_records_is_zero and test_cli_empty_summary. Related run `-k average`: 4 passed, 0 failed.
verification.full_suite: 44 passed, 30 failed of 74 after this fix. In tests/test_app.py 5 tests fail, all of which failed at baseline; no baseline-passing test regressed.

bugs.title: total_valid_transactions adds refunds instead of subtracting them
bugs.expected: The net total is the sum of the signed amounts; a refund lowers the total. Example: 100.0, -30.0, 50.0 total 120.0. Sample data net total is 501.25.
bugs.actual: Each refund is added as a positive amount.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_app.py::test_total_subtracts_refunds tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k 'total_subtracts_refunds or bh004 or cli_summary'
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED. Existing test: 280.0 instead of 220.0. Spec example 100.0, -30.0, 50.0 gave 180.0 instead of 120.0. Refunds -20.0 and -5.5 gave 25.5 instead of -25.5. CLI summary printed net total 541.25 instead of 501.25.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 65 adds abs(tx['amount']), discarding the sign that marks a refund. Symptom: totals too high by twice the refund amount; CLI summary net total 541.25 instead of 501.25.

fix.summary: total_valid_transactions adds the signed amount (`tx["amount"]`) instead of `abs(tx["amount"])`.

verification.targeted: PASSED (4 passed): tests/test_app.py::test_total_subtracts_refunds, test_bh004_total_spec_example, test_bh004_total_of_only_refunds_is_negative and test_cli_summary_with_sample_data. Related run `-k total`: 5 passed, 0 failed.
verification.full_suite: 48 passed, 26 failed of 74 after this fix. In tests/test_app.py 4 tests fail, all of which failed at baseline; no baseline-passing test regressed.

bugs.title: get_transaction raises or returns the wrong record for an invalid index
bugs.expected: Returns None when index is not an integer, is negative, or is >= count(); never raises.
bugs.actual: IndexError for an index past either end, TypeError for a non-integer index, and a record counted from the end for an in-range negative index.
bugs.evidence: Line 59 `return self._transactions[index]` indexes the list directly with no checks.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_app.py tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k 'get_transaction_out_of_range or get_transaction_negative or bh005 or cli_show_out_of_range'
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED. Index 10, index == count(), index 0 on an empty store and index -5 raised IndexError; index -1 returned the last record; indexes '1', 1.5, None and [0] raised TypeError; `app.py show 99` raised IndexError.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 59 indexes the list directly, so Python list semantics apply (negative indexes count from the end, out-of-range raises IndexError, non-integers raise TypeError) instead of the specified 'return None'. Symptom: exceptions from get_transaction and a traceback from `app.py show 99`.

fix.summary: get_transaction returns None unless index is an int with 0 <= index < the number of stored records; the list is indexed only after that check.

verification.targeted: PASSED (10 passed): the two existing tests test_get_transaction_out_of_range_returns_none and test_get_transaction_negative_index_returns_none, the seven test_bh005_* cases and test_cli_show_out_of_range_position. Related run `-k 'get_transaction or cli_show'`: 13 passed, 0 failed.
verification.full_suite: 58 passed, 16 failed of 74 after this fix. In tests/test_app.py 2 tests fail, both of which failed at baseline; no baseline-passing test regressed.

bugs.notes: A bool index is still accepted as position 0 or 1 because bool is a subclass of int; the specification does not say whether a bool is 'an integer' here (see observations).

bugs.title: apply_discount accepts a percent below 0 or above 100
bugs.expected: A percent below 0 or above 100 raises ValueError; 0 returns the amount unchanged and 100 returns 0.0.
bugs.actual: Any percent is accepted and a result is returned.
bugs.evidence: Lines 52-53 compute and return the result with no range check on percent.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_app.py tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k 'apply_discount_rejects or bh006'
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED: DID NOT RAISE ValueError for percent 150, -10, 100.01, 1000, -0.01 and -100.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: apply_discount never checks percent before computing, so the range rule in the specification is simply not implemented. Symptom: negative or inflated prices returned instead of ValueError.

fix.summary: apply_discount raises ValueError when percent is not between 0 and 100 inclusive, before computing the discount. The check is written `not 0 <= percent <= 100`, so a NaN percent is rejected as well (it is not 'between 0 and 100 inclusive').

verification.targeted: PASSED (6 passed): tests/test_app.py::test_apply_discount_rejects_percent_above_100, test_apply_discount_rejects_negative_percent and the four test_bh006_* cases. Related run `-k discount`: 9 passed, 0 failed (includes the 0 and 100 boundary test and the CLI `discount 200 15` test).
verification.full_suite: 64 passed, 10 failed of 74 after this fix. All 18 tests in tests/test_app.py pass; the 10 remaining failures are the BH-007 and BH-008 reproductions.

bugs.title: validate_transaction accepts any three-character currency (lowercase, digits, symbols, non-ASCII)
bugs.expected: currency must be exactly three uppercase ASCII letters; each broken rule adds one problem.
bugs.expected_behaviour_source: demo-app/EXPECTED_BEHAVIOUR.md data model table, `currency` row (line 14) and `validate_transaction` third bullet (lines 36-37)
bugs.actual: Any three-character string is accepted as a currency.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k bh007
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED. validate_transaction returned [] for currencies 'usd', 'Usd', '123', 'U$D', 'US ' and 'ÄÖÜ'; a record with currency 'usd' was returned by valid_transactions(); add_transaction stored it without raising.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 39 checks only the type and length of currency; the 'uppercase ASCII letters' part of the rule is not implemented. Symptom: records with malformed currencies count as valid and enter totals, averages and duplicate detection, and add_transaction stores them.

bugs.title: validate_transaction raises OverflowError for an int amount too large to convert to float
bugs.expected: validate_transaction never raises. An int amount is finite by definition, so a non-zero int breaks no rule in the data model.
bugs.expected_behaviour_source: demo-app/EXPECTED_BEHAVIOUR.md `validate_transaction` last bullet 'Never raises' (line 38) and data model table `amount` row (line 13)
bugs.actual: Raises OverflowError for an int amount that cannot be converted to a float.
bugs.evidence: Line 33 `elif math.isnan(amount) or math.isinf(amount)` is reached for ints as well as floats.

reproduction.command: cd demo-app && python3 -m pytest tests/test_bug_hunter_regressions.py -k bh008
reproduction.result_before_fix: FAILED with OverflowError: int too large to convert to float at utils.py:33, for amounts 10**400 and -(10**400).

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 33 calls math.isnan/math.isinf on int amounts; those functions convert their argument to a C double, which overflows for ints beyond the float range. Only floats can be NaN or infinite. Symptom: OverflowError from validate_transaction and from everything that calls it (is_valid_transaction, add_transaction, valid_transactions and all calculations).

fix.summary: validate_transaction applies the NaN/infinity check only to float amounts (`isinstance(amount, float) and (...)`); an int is always finite, so it goes straight to the zero check.

verification.targeted: PASSED (2 passed): both parameters of test_bh008_validate_does_not_raise_for_an_int_too_large_for_a_float. Related run `-k 'validate or amount'`: 29 passed, 0 failed (includes the NaN, inf, -inf, bool, zero and non-numeric amount cases, which are still rejected).
verification.full_suite: 74 passed, 0 failed of 74 after this fix.

bugs.notes: Decision for the user: the fix follows the letter of the data model (a non-zero int is valid however large). The alternative reading, that an amount which cannot be a float should be reported as a problem, would also satisfy 'never raises' and would make BH-009 disappear. See BH-009.

bugs.title: average_transaction_value raises OverflowError when a valid amount is an int too large for a float
bugs.location: TransactionService.average_transaction_value, lines 43-44 (also total_valid_transactions line 65 and utils.round_money line 10)
bugs.expected: average_transaction_value never raises for a store that holds only dictionaries.
bugs.expected_behaviour_source: demo-app/EXPECTED_BEHAVIOUR.md section `average_transaction_value()` second bullet (line 88). No source says what value to return when the mean cannot be represented as a float.
bugs.actual: Observed at baseline with one stored record whose amount is 10**400: average_transaction_value() and total_valid_transactions() both raised OverflowError, raised from utils.py line 33 (the BH-008 root cause), not yet from the calculation itself. Observed again after the BH-008 fix: the record is now valid, average_transaction_value() raises OverflowError: integer division result too large for a float at transaction_service.py line 46, and total_valid_transactions() raises OverflowError: int too large to convert to float at transaction_service.py line 69.

reproduction.test: none added (no source for the expected return value)
reproduction.command: one-off python3 snippet run from demo-app: load a single record with amount 10**400, then call average_transaction_value() and total_valid_transactions()
reproduction.result_before_fix: Both calls raised OverflowError: int too large to convert to float, at utils.py line 33.

bugs.notes: Unresolved (needs specification). The specification says average_transaction_value never raises for a store that holds only dictionaries, but gives no value to return when the mean of valid amounts cannot be represented as a float, and it is silent on whether total_valid_transactions may raise. Choosing a return value, or declaring such amounts invalid, is a judgement call for the user. At baseline this failure is a secondary failure of BH-008. After the BH-008 fix it is an independent failure in the calculations (observed with a one-off snippet, no test added). No code was changed for this defect.

observations.summary: get_transaction(True) / get_transaction(False): bool is a subclass of int in Python, so a bool index would be treated as position 1 / 0.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The specification says only 'not an integer'. It excludes bool explicitly for `amount` but says nothing for `index`, so whether a bool counts as an integer here is a judgement call.

observations.summary: `python3 app.py discount 200 150` has no specified output. Once apply_discount raises ValueError as specified, the CLI will end with an uncaught ValueError traceback.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The app.py table in the specification does not define the CLI behaviour for an out-of-range percent. Needs the user's decision.

observations.summary: format_transaction would raise for a record with a non-numeric amount (format spec `>10.2f`) or a non-dictionary record.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The CLI only loads the built-in sample data, which contains no such record, and the specification does not define the output for one. Hypothetical.

observations.summary: TransactionService.__init__ accepts an optional `transactions` argument and stores it without validation.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The constructor argument is not described in the specification; nothing documented contradicts it.

observations.summary: Missing test coverage: app.py (the CLI) has no tests at all; the specification's command table is unchecked.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: Missing coverage, not a defect in itself. CLI failures are secondary symptoms of the service defects.

observations.summary: Missing test coverage: add_transaction storing a copy, load/count/all_transactions/valid_transactions, round_money, discount boundaries 0 and 100, the id whitespace rule, bool/NaN/inf amounts, non-dictionary input to validate_transaction.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: Reading the code, these rules appear to hold; they are untested.

observations.summary: find_duplicates, all_transactions, valid_transactions and get_transaction return the stored dictionary objects themselves, so a caller that mutates a returned record changes the store.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The specification asks for a new list, not for copies of the records, and says only that find_duplicates itself must not change the stored records. Hypothetical risk.
